title: Two Sum
description:
Given n integers and a target, print the 0-based indices of the two numbers that add up to target (smaller index first).

Input: first line n, second line n integers, third line target.
Output: two indices separated by a space.

examples.explanation: nums[0] + nums[1] == 9, so the answer is 0 1.

title: Add Two Numbers
description:
Two non-negative integers are given as lists of digits stored in reverse order (least significant digit first). Add them and print the sum in the same reversed-digit form.

Input: n1, then n1 digits; n2, then n2 digits.
Output: the digits of the sum, space separated, in reverse order.
constraints: No leading zeros, except the number 0 itself.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description:
Given a string s, print the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

Input: one line containing s (may contain spaces).
Output: a single integer.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description:
Given two sorted arrays, print the median of the merged array with exactly 5 digits after the decimal point.

Input: m, then m integers (empty line if m = 0); n, then n integers (empty line if n = 0).
Output: the median, e.g. 2.00000

title: Container With Most Water
description:
Given n vertical lines with heights h[0..n-1] (line i at x = i), find two lines that together with the x-axis hold the most water and print that area.

Input: n, then n heights.
Output: the maximum area.

examples.explanation: The best pair is index 1 and 8 (heights 8 and 7): min(8,7) * 7 = 49.

title: 3Sum
description:
Find all unique triplets in the array that sum to 0.

Input: n, then n integers.
Output: first line k = number of unique triplets. Then k lines, each a triplet in ascending order. Triplets themselves are printed in ascending (lexicographic) order.

title: Group Anagrams
description:
Group the words that are anagrams of each other.

Input: n, then n lowercase words on one line (space separated).
Output: one line per group. Words inside a group are sorted alphabetically, and groups are ordered by their first word.

examples.input:
6
eat tea tan ate nat bat
examples.output:
ate eat tea
bat
nat tan
examples.explanation: Three groups: ate eat tea / bat / nat tan.

constraints: Words consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
description:
Print the k most frequent elements of the array in ascending order.

Input: n, then n integers, then k.
Output: k integers, space separated, ascending.

examples.explanation: 1 appears 3 times and 2 appears 2 times, so the top 2 are 1 and 2.

constraints: The answer is guaranteed to be unique.

title: Product of Array Except Self
description:
For each index i, print the product of all elements except nums[i]. Do not use division.

Input: n, then n integers.
Output: n integers, space separated.
constraints: Every prefix/suffix product fits in a 32-bit integer.

title: Course Schedule
description:
There are n courses labeled 0..n-1 and p prerequisite pairs "a b" meaning you must take course b before course a. Print true if all courses can be finished, otherwise false.

Input: first line n and p, then p lines each with a b.
Output: true or false.

examples.explanation: To take course 1 you must finish course 0 first, which is possible.

title: Sum of Two Numbers
description:
Read two integers and print their sum.

Input: one line with two integers a and b.
Output: a + b.

title: Check Palindrome
description:
Given a lowercase string, print YES if it reads the same forwards and backwards, otherwise NO.

Input: one line with the string s.
Output: YES or NO.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.
